mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) from the prior month to the current month signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS declined from the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a dual shock of economic weakness and restrictive monetary policy, which amplifies equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS rise from the prior month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a simultaneous peak in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals overheating, leading to a market correction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in late-cycle expansion periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past quarter signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods of rising PAYEMS, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where CPIAUCSL yoy > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production (INDPRO) from the prior month signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) in periods of rising INDPRO, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a high unemployment regime that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) in periods where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
